notes: S122-01. Scan 122 is author page 60 with a separate lower-left pencil 121. The line count is 22 main writing baselines, counting the separate descriptive baselines in displays but not raised insertions or marginal numbers. The whole page, both native halves, and all 20 saved first-pass crops were read visually. No OCR, external sources, other-page files, or compilation were used.

S122-02. The opening paragraph calls T^!_d the inverse image of T_d on D^!_d and reports an action of the broad-S group; it presents the quotient expression with two waves above a straight bar. These are manuscript assertions reported as written, not proof-checked conclusions.

S122-03. The page introduces d indexed connectors s_i, an immersion hypothesis, the canonical invertible normal sheaf L_1, the pullbacks L_{d,i}, associated torsors and their product. This records the construction claimed on the leaf; no proof of regularity, normal-sheaf invertibility, or equivariance was independently established.

S122-04. Each of the eight decorated occurrences was checked independently: T at the start; D in the first sur, quotient, Or sur, (185), considérer sur and conclusion; and P in (189). All have a stem and a detached point. Conversely, the D_d base in the torseurs sous line, both D_d occurrences on the right of (188), and final live P_d have no bang. The latter forms are retained.

S122-05. A local type/index-consistency check uses only the written s_i source and L_{d,i}=s_i^*(L_1): these place the pullback on D^!_d, while the associated-torsor text writes D_d. The page does not state the intermediate descent or identification needed to reconcile those bases. The bare final P_d could name a descended object or reflect omitted decoration; neither possibility licenses changing the clear ink. This is a notation/type check, not a targeted proof check.

S122-06. Both short horizontal connectors are drawn with their small downward terminal turns. The crop does not supply two clear sides of an arrowhead. The transcription preserves geometry and leaves directional interpretation open; mathematical need was not used to complete a head.

S122-07. The stroke beneath régulière is connected to g and only extends left beneath the beginning of the word. The partial TikZ stroke approximates that visible extent without claiming an exact boundary between printed letters; intentional emphasis and a long descender remain unresolved. The independent underline beneath normal is retained.

S122-08. The (188) group base is set lower than m using grouped subscripting, with no added comma or parentheses. This is a placement check against both witnesses, not a mathematical correction. In (189) the final point supplied by H is absent; the concluding sentence has no new point at the page edge.

S122-09. All four C deletions and all five C insertions, including the raised sur D_1 inside the canceled revision, were checked separately. The two short final strikes cross qui and devient; de replaces qui from above, and the live façon is outside the second strike. The terminal point beside the uncertain canceled faisceau is retained as part of that canceled phrase.

S122-10. Four indexed C choices are resolved to the broad curled S form. The unindexed canceled faisceau doubt is retained, and the canceled rev letters are newly marked uncertain with their clear point outside the uncertainty wrapper. The lower-left 121 is actual pencil writing and therefore receives an H-omission row; H’s editorial introductory note is not source text.
